title: Check which disk is full, including inode use
summary: Show how much space is free on each disk and how many file slots (inodes) are free. This tells you whether a disk is full by size or by number of files. All commands in this card only read information and change nothing.

aliases.text: linux no space left on device
linux disk full but few files
как посмотреть свободное место на диске linux
no space left on device linux проверить

steps.explain: Show the size, used space and free space of every mounted disk or partition. Sizes use human units such as G and M. Read-only.
steps.expect: A table with Filesystem, Size, Used, Avail, Use% and Mounted on. Look for a row with Use% at 90% or more, for example 100% on /.

alternatives.explain: Hide temporary and virtual filesystems so only real disks are listed. Read-only.
alternatives.expect: The same table without tmpfs and devtmpfs rows.

steps.explain: Show how many inodes (file slots) are used and free on every filesystem. A disk can be full because it holds too many files even when it still has free bytes. Read-only.
steps.expect: A table with Inodes, IUsed, IFree, IUse% and Mounted on. If IUse% is 100% while Use% in the previous step is low, the disk is full by file count.

alternatives.explain: Show the same inode table with exact numbers instead of human units. Read-only.
alternatives.expect: Exact counts in the IUsed and IFree columns.

steps.explain: List disks and partitions with their filesystem type and mount point. Use it to match a Mounted on name from df, such as /home, with a device name, such as /dev/sda2. Read-only.
steps.expect: A tree of disks and partitions with FSTYPE and MOUNTPOINTS columns. The partition mounted on / is the root disk.

verify.expect: One data row ending with / in the Mounted on column, with a Use% value.

warnings: Rows named tmpfs or devtmpfs are memory-based virtual filesystems. A 100% value on them is normal and does not mean your disk is full.

source.title: df manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
